author: John O'Sullivan & Bradley Jolly
title: Donald Trump booed as he takes seat at Les Miserables after 'woke' criticism - NewsBreak
text: The tense atmosphere was palpable as grainy footage showed audience members booing and jeering at Donald Trump as the President settled into his seat for the opening night of 'Les Misérables. ' Several cast members were reportedly considering skipping out on Wednesday's performance at the prestigious John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington DC, knowing that Trump would be in attendance. The former President had stirred up tension with those in the arts community when he pushed for significant changes earlier in the year after controversially being elected chairman. These changes aggressively targeted what he labeled "woke" productions, like drag shows. READ MORE: Paul McCartney's 3-word message to city as he joins Bruce Springsteen onstage READ MORE: 'Best war movie ever' that's likened to Saving Private Ryan remains largely unknown As Trump, alongside First Lady Melania, made their appearance in the auditorium before the start of 'Les Mis,' you could almost cut the dissatisfaction with a knife. This marked Trump's first visit to the national cultural center since his reelection and the sweeping changes that followed. Noticeably unoccupied spaces dotted the balconies and orchestra section, fueling rumors that some attendees chose to skip the performance in protest. It's believed that understudies stepped in for principal actors, who also elected to stay away due to the controversy surrounding Trump's attendance, reports the Mirror . The Mirror is looking into verifying these claims - including how many performers actually pulled out. Despite a decline in subscription package sales and cancellations of several touring productions, including Hamilton, since Mr. Trump's takeover, the former president remained proud as he attended a performance on Wednesday. Dressed in a tuxedo, Mr. Trump, who has a fondness for Les Misérables, enjoyed the musical set in 19th-century France. He has even played its songs at his events, including Do You Hear the People Sing? a revolutionary anthem inspired by the 1832 rebellion against the French king. Vice President JD Vance and his wife, Usha, were also present. Ric Grenell, the Trump-appointed interim leader of the Kennedy Center, stood nearby as the President spoke to reporters. Attorney General Pam Bondi mingled with other guests, while Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr took selfies with attendees. However, the MAGA takeover was met with jeers from the audience. Social media users pointed out the irony of Mr. Trump choosing to watch a performance about a mass uprising against a tyrannical king. Photos shared online showed audience members dressed in drag, a nod to Mr. Trump's criticism of the venue hosting drag shows prior to his takeover. Despite this, some reports suggest a minority in the audience cheered the President's arrival. Upon hearing from reporters that some cast members might have bailed because of him, the unfazed world leader, Mr Trump, remarked: "I couldn't care less."
